title: Nonlinear stability of subextremal Kerr black holes

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'We settle the global nonlinear stability problem for the family of Kerr black holes in the full subextremal range: spacetimes evolving from initial data close to those of a subextremal Kerr black hole as solutions of the Einstein vacuum equation Ric(g)=0 settle down to a nearby member of the Kerr family at the rate O(t_*^{-2-eps}) in spatially compact regions. For the initial data, we require O(r^{-1-eps_0})-decay for eps_0>0 ... We work directly with the tensorial equation ...' Comments: 339 pages, 21 figures. v2: fixed typos, updated references, improved exposition.

notes: Preprint, no journal ref as of 2026-09-11. This is the strongest available discharge of the Kerr-stability antecedent in T-301/T-515. Must be tracked for peer review.

title: Constraint damping on subextremal Kerr spacetimes

verification.evidence: Abstract: '...we show that an enhanced form of constraint damping can be implemented for the linearization of the Einstein equations around any subextremal Kerr black hole metric. The results proved here are a key ingredient in the author's proof of the nonlinear stability of the subextremal Kerr family.'

title: The formation of a weak null singularity in the interior of generic rotating black holes

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'Given a characteristic initial value problem with smooth data representing a dynamical event horizon settling down to that of Kerr in the subextremal, strictly rotating range with suitable upper and lower bounds, we prove that a weak null singularity forms, across which the spacetime metric is continuously extendible but not Lipschitz extendible. The bulk of the proof is a stability argument showing that a dynamical Teukolsky field can be approximated by a linear Teukolsky field, whose linear instability was proved in previous works.'

notes: KEY RESULT: nonlinear vacuum, no symmetry, strictly rotating subextremal Kerr; C^0-extendible but NOT Lipschitz-extendible. Preprint (v1). This plus SRC-081 covers the C^2 formulation at preprint level for a class of generic rotating interiors.

title: Lipschitz inextendibility of weak null singularities from curvature blow-up
venue: arXiv:2409.18838 (v2, Nov 2025), 25 pages; accepted for publication in Inventiones Mathematicae (per arXiv comment)

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'We prove the C^{0,1}_loc-inextendibility of weak null singularities without any symmetry assumptions. The proof introduces a new strategy to infer C^{0,1}_loc-inextendibility from the blow-up of curvature. The assumed blow-up is expected to be satisfied for weak null singularities in the interior of generic rotating black holes. Thus, we expect the result presented here to directly contribute to the resolution of the C^{0,1}_loc-formulation of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in a neighbourhood of subextremal Kerr.' Comments: v2: 25 pages, 4 figures, significantly expanded version ... Version accepted for publication in Inventiones Mathematicae.

notes: Peer-reviewed acceptance stated in the arXiv comment (Invent. Math.); final volume/pages not yet machine-confirmed. Symmetry-free criterion; applies conditional on the curvature blow-up being satisfied (now supplied for characteristic data by SRC-080).

title: A note on the instability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon under linearised gravitational perturbations

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'This note slightly strengthens the result of arXiv:2201.12295 on the linear instability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon. This strengthened result is used in the proof arXiv:2604.04877 of the non-linear instability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon.'

title: Precise asymptotics of the spin +2 Teukolsky field in the Kerr black hole interior

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'Using a purely physical-space analysis, we prove the precise oscillatory blow-up asymptotics of the spin +2 Teukolsky field in the interior of a subextremal Kerr black hole. In particular, this work gives a new proof of the blueshift instability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon against linearized gravitational perturbations ... In that sense, this work supports the Strong Cosmic Censorship conjecture in Kerr spacetimes.' Journal ref: Commun. Math. Phys. 406 (2025) 152; DOI 10.1007/s00220-025-05332-3.

title: Generic linearized curvature singularity at the perturbed Kerr Cauchy horizon

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'We prove the precise asymptotics of the spin -2 Teukolsky field in the interior and along the Cauchy horizon of a subextremal Kerr black hole. Together with the oscillatory blow-up asymptotics of the spin +2 Teukolsky field proven in our previous work, our result suggests that generic perturbations of a Kerr black hole build up to form a coordinate-independent curvature singularity at the Cauchy horizon. This supports the Strong Cosmic Censorship conjecture in Kerr spacetimes.'

notes: Linearized level; 'suggests', not proves, a curvature singularity.

title: Instability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon under linearised gravitational perturbations
venue: Annals of PDE (accepted per arXiv comment); arXiv:2201.12295 (v2)

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'This paper establishes a mathematical proof of the blue-shift instability at the sub-extremal Kerr Cauchy horizon for the linearised vacuum Einstein equations. More precisely, we exhibit conditions on the s=+2 Teukolsky field, consisting of suitable integrated upper and lower bounds on the decay along the event horizon, that ensure that the Teukolsky field, with respect to a frame that is regular at the Cauchy horizon, becomes singular. The conditions are in particular satisfied by solutions of the Teukolsky equation arising from generic and compactly supported initial data by the recent work [51] of Ma and Zhang for slowly rotating Kerr.' Comments: 102 pages; v2 accepted for publication in Annals of PDE.

notes: Linearised vacuum gravity; input to SRC-080.
